arxiv-1902-06695.title: The limit of the Riemann zeta function and its nontrivial zeros
arxiv-1902-06695.creator: Tanfer Tanriverdi
arxiv-1902-06695.description: Abstract In this article, with a new approach, which is not discussed in the literature yet, the limit of the Riemann zeta function or Euler-Riemann zeta function is approximately explored by applying Dirichlet’s rearrangement theorem for absolutely convergent series to the Riemann zeta function by rearranging its terms as geometric series for sufficiently large n n .

arxiv-1912-04896.title: Self Organizing Nebulous Growths for Robust and Incremental Data Visualization
arxiv-1912-04896.creator: Damith A. Senanayake, Wei Wang, Shalin H. Naik, Saman Halgamuge
arxiv-1912-04896.description: Abstract Non-parametric dimensionality reduction techniques, such as t-SNE and UMAP, are proficient in providing visualizations for datasets of fixed sizes. However, they cannot incrementally map and insert new data points into an already provided data visualization. arxiv-2012-05648.title: Towards a global dynamic wind atlas: A multi-country validation of wind power simulation from MERRA-2 and ERA-5 reanalyses bias-corrected with the Global Wind Atlas
arxiv-2012-05648.creator: Katharina Gruber, Peter Regner, Sebastian Wehrle, Marianne Zeyringer, Johannes Schmidt
arxiv-2012-05648.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Katharina Gruber, Peter Regner, Sebastian Wehrle, Marianne Zeyringer, Johannes Schmidt. Reanalysis data are widely used for simulating renewable energy and in particular wind power generation. While MERRA-2 has been a de-facto standard in many studies, the newer ERA5- reanalysis recently gained importance. Here, we use these two datasets to simulate wind power generation and evaluate the respective quality in terms of correlations and errors when validated against historical wind power generation.

arxiv-2012-15708.title: Geometry of the Wiman–Edge monodromy
arxiv-2012-15708.creator: Matthew Stover
arxiv-2012-15708.description: Abstract The Wiman–Edge pencil is a pencil of genus 6 6 curves for which the generic member has automorphism group the alternating group 𝔄 5 \mathfrak{A}_{5} . There is a unique smooth member, the Wiman sextic , with automorphism group the symmetric group 𝔖 5 \mathfrak{S}_{5} .

arxiv-2106-13124.title: Moore machines duality
arxiv-2106-13124.creator: Jacques Peyrière
arxiv-2106-13124.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jacques Peyrière. We present a simple algorithm to find the Moore machine with the minimun number of states equivalent to a given one. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 2020 classification: 68Q45, 68Q70, 03D05 1. Introduction It is known that there is a unique, up to isomorphism, deterministic finite automaton with a minimum number of states which recognizes the same language as a given one.

arxiv-2302-07509.title: Automated Movement Detection with Dirichlet Process Mixture Models and Electromyography
arxiv-2302-07509.creator: Navin Cooray, Zhenglin Li, Jinzhuo Wang, Christine Lo, Mahnaz Arvaneh, Mkael Symmonds, Michele Hu, Maarten De Vos, Lyudmila S Mihaylova
arxiv-2302-07509.description: Abstract Numerous sleep disorders are characterised by movement during sleep, these include rapid-eye movement sleep behaviour disorder (RBD) and periodic limb movement disorder. The process of diagnosing movement related sleep disorders requires laborious and time-consuming visual analysis of sleep recordings. This process involves sleep clinicians visually inspecting electromyogram (EMG) signals to identify abnormal movements.

arxiv-2302-13081.title: Isolated Suborders and their Application to Counting Closure Operators
arxiv-2302-13081.creator: Roland Glück ORCID:0000-0001-7909-1942
arxiv-2302-13081.description: Abstract . In this paper, we investigate the interplay between isolated suborders and closures. Isolated suborders are a special kind of suborders and can be used to diminish the number of elements of an ordered set by means of a quotient construction.

arxiv-2311-14963.title: Precision spectrophotometry for PNLF distances: the case of NGC 300
arxiv-2311-14963.creator: Azlizan A. Soemitro 1,2, Martin M. Roth 1,2, Peter M. Weilbacher 1, Robin Ciardullo 3, George H. Jacoby 4, Ana Monreal-Ibero 5, Norberto Castro 1, Genoveva Micheva 1
arxiv-2311-14963.description: Abstract The Multi-Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) has enabled a renaissance of the planetary nebula luminosity function (PNLF) as a standard candle. In the case of NGC 300, we learned that the precise spectrophotometry of MUSE was crucial to obtain an accurate PNLF distance.

arxiv-2402-04433.creator: Fabrizio Ghezzi, Eduardo Rossi, Lorenzo Trapani
arxiv-2402-04433.description: Abstract . We study online changepoint detection in the context of a linear regression model. We propose a class of heavily weighted statistics based on the CUSUM process of the regression residuals, which are specifically designed to ensure timely detection of breaks occurring early on during the monitoring horizon.

arxiv-2511-11654.title: Convergence of Multiagent Learning Systems for Traffic control
arxiv-2511-11654.creator: Sayambhu Sen, Shalabh Bhatnagar
arxiv-2511-11654.description: Abstract Rapid urbanization in cities like Bangalore has led to severe traffic congestion, making efficient Traffic Signal Control (TSC) essential. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), often modeling each traffic signal as an independent agent using Q-learning, has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce average commuter delays.

Behavioral studies of Caenorhabditis elegans traditionally are done on the smooth surface of agar plates, but the natural habitat of C. elegans and other nematodes is the soil, a complex and structured environment. In order to investigate how worms move in such environments, we h

pmc-10835404.title: Optimizing nitrogen and phosphorus application to improve soil organic carbon and alfalfa hay yield in alfalfa fields
pmc-10835404.creator: Kongqin Wei, Junwei Zhao, Yanliang Sun, Ignacio F. López, Chunhui Ma, Qianbing Zhang
pmc-10835404.description: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is the principal factor contributing to enhanced soil fertility and also functions as the major carbon sink within terrestrial ecosystems. Applying fertilizer is a crucial agricultural practice that enhances SOC and promotes crop yields. Nevertheless, the response of SOC, active organic carbon fraction and hay yield to nitrogen and phosphorus application is still unclear.

pmc-11550586.title: ReflACTION framework: A proposed model for implementation of clinical pharmacy services
pmc-11550586.creator: Kérilin Stancine Santos Rocha, Sabrina Cerqueira-Santos, Genival Araújo dos Santos-Júnior, Lincoln Marques Cavalcante-Santos, Fernando de Castro Araújo-Neto, Fernanda Oliveira Prado, Giselle de Carvalho Brito, Divaldo Pereira de Lyra-Jr.
pmc-11550586.description: The implementation of clinical pharmacy services (CPS) has grown worldwide. However, few studies have used models and/or frameworks to facilitate the implementation process, especially in a low and middle-income countries. In addition, there are limitations in the ways that implementation frameworks are used. Therefore, this discussion aimed to propose and describe an approach using the ReflACTION framework.

pmc-11689592.title: SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND AGING: A US–ENGLAND COMPARATIVE STUDY OF SAME-SEX AND DIFFERENT-SEX HOUSEHOLDS
pmc-11689592.creator: Ariel Azar, Laia Becares, Dylan Kneale
pmc-11689592.description: This study compares the health, income, and housing situation of same-sex and opposite-sex households in the United States and England. The research uses data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) and the U.S. Health and Retirement Study (HRS) to examine how these inequalities change over time.

pmc-12452481.title: Future directions in combating outbreaks at CEPI Centralized Laboratory Network
pmc-12452481.creator: Ali Azizi, Gathoni Kamuyu, Peter Spencer, Valentina Bernasconi
pmc-12452481.description: The first CEPI Centralized Laboratory Network (CLN) meeting held in Rome in July 2024 gathered 67 experts from 27 global institutions, including CLN facilities, alongside key collaborators such as the World Health Organization (WHO), European Commission, US Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA), Gates Foundation, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), PATH, and the Pasteur Network.

pmc-12595744.title: Externalizing behaviors in children living near coal-fired power plants
pmc-12595744.creator: Kristina M. Zierold, John V. Myers, Guy N. Brock, Charlie H. Zhang, Lonnie Sears
pmc-12595744.description: BackgroundProximity to coal-fired plants exposes children to neurotoxic metals, which can negatively impact their behavioral health. Our research team previously reported an association between coal fly ash exposure and depression. However, other neurobehavioral outcomes have not been assessed. We hypothesized that the presence of fly ash would be associated with increased externalizing behaviors in children aged 6–14 years old.

pmc-12690052.title: Patient Experience of Inpatient Care: Insights From a Multicentered Study in Ghanaian Hospitals
pmc-12690052.creator: Veronica Penaman Asamoah, Emmanuel Kumah, Michael Afari Baidoo, Samuel Egyakwa Ankomah, Adam Fusheini, Samuel Kofi Agyei
pmc-12690052.description: Background: Patient experience is a key indicator of healthcare quality, influencing satisfaction, safety, and outcomes. In Ghana, limited research has examined inpatient experiences across diverse settings. This study explored patient experiences of inpatient care and examined how these experiences relate to patient characteristics in public hospitals.

pmc-13099975.title: 24-week multidimensional predictors of return to play post-ACLR in high-sports demanders: a randomized trial
pmc-13099975.creator: Feng Hao, Niu Yuhong, Yang Xuyuan, Cui Mu, Li Qiangze
pmc-13099975.description: Predicting successful return to play (RTP) during mid-stage rehabilitation after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) remains a critical, unresolved clinical challenge. High-sports demanders (HSDs)—non-professional athletes participating in level-1 sports (cutting, pivoting, jumping) ≥ 3 times/week with Tegner score > 5—represent a distinct subgroup who face unique rehabilitation challenges yet lack evidence-based mid-stage prediction tools.

pmc-13222607.title: Genetic and Epigenetic Association of Lung Function and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease-Related Phenotypes in the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study: A Scoping Review
pmc-13222607.creator: Sun Young Kang, Sanghyun Roh, Jeong-An Gim
pmc-13222607.description: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is influenced by environmental exposure and genetic susceptibility. Although large-scale genetic studies have identified loci associated with COPD and lung function, most evidence has come from populations of European ancestry, and data from Asian populations remain limited.

pmc-13242959.title: Beyond a simple oxidation reaction: the complex molecular network regulating fruit and vegetable browning
pmc-13242959.creator: Jia Guo, Xinyi Duan, He Xu, Zishan Xu, Alisdair R Fernie, Yanjie Zhang
pmc-13242959.description: Fruit and vegetable browning is a complex physiological phenomenon responsible for substantial postharvest losses and profound economic consequences. While enzymatic oxidation mediated by oxidative enzymes has long been considered the core mechanism, emerging evidence highlights the flavonoid pathway as an alternative route, influencing pigmentation outcomes.

pmc-13353910.title: Performance of DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT-5 in the Generation of North American Spine Society Clinical Guidelines for Adult Vertebral Compression Fractures: Comparative Study
pmc-13353910.creator: Ruiyuan Chen, Yue Pan, Minghui Liang, Aobo Wang, Ziqian Ma, Yu Xi, Ning Fan, Shuo Yuan, Peng Du, Tianyi Wang, Lei Zang
pmc-13353910.description: BackgroundVertebral compression fractures (VCFs) impose a substantial clinical and health care burden, and their management relies on timely access to evidence-based guidelines. Large language models (LLMs) may help clinicians rapidly obtain guideline-related information, but their performance on VCF guidelines remains unclear.

pmc-13356074.title: Fissure locations and fire-fountain dynamics during the December 2023–September 2024 Svartsengi Volcanic System eruptions, Iceland, from aerial imagery and recreational webcam footage
pmc-13356074.creator: Rebekah S Rhodes, David M Pyle, Tamsin A Mather, Gro B M Pedersen, Michelle M Parks
pmc-13356074.description: Recent fissure-fed eruptions from the Svartsengi Volcanic System have significantly impacted Iceland’s Reykjanes Peninsula. With eruptions likely to continue intermittently for decades to centuries, exploring the controls on the locations of fissure-fed eruptions is important for hazard assessment and risk mitigation.

pmc-13480832.title: π‐Extended COUPY Fluorophores for Targeted Near‐Infrared Fluorescence and Lifetime Imaging in Live Cells
pmc-13480832.creator: Diego Abad‐Montero, Manel Bosch, Rodrigo Garcés‐Castellanos, Michael Q. Schottenhamel, Sergio Pedraza‐Arevalo, Alejandro Ibáñez‐Costa, Justo P. Castaño, Tania García‐Becerra, Elena Rebollo, Marta E. Alberto, Antonio Francés‐Monerris, Vicente Marchán

pmc-13518768.title: Metal electrodes transfer using polycarbonate for the fabrication of molybdenum disulfide semiconductor devices
pmc-13518768.creator: Chih-Hao Chiang, Ruo-Yao Wang, Jing-Ting Chou, Yun-Ping Chiu, Che-Wei Chu, Yueh-Wei Chen, Guan-Ting Chen, Zi-Rui Su, Chi Chen, Chen-Fang Kang, Jhong-Ren Huang, Meng-Lin Tsai
pmc-13518768.description: Fabricating high-performance 2D nanosheet-based semiconductor devices faces challenges due to the structural damage caused by traditional metal electrode deposition processes. This study introduces a novel polycarbonate (PC) assisted metal electrode transfer technique that effectively preserves the structural and electronic properties of MoS2 nanosheets.

uslaw-usc-t42-s4391.title: 42 U.S.C. § 4391 — Congressional statement of findings
uslaw-usc-t42-s4391.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s4391.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 57 (Environmental Pollution Study). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Congress finds that there is general agreement that air, water, and other common environmental pollution may be hazardous to the health of individuals resident in the United States, but that despite the existence of various research papers and other technical reports.
